newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia says coffee exports up 4,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia says coffee exports up 4,000 tonnes.

text.p: Ethiopia exported 36,907 tonnes of coffee worth $92 million in the first three months of the 1996/97 (October/September) crop year, an official said on Saturday.
Tsegaye Berhane, general manager of the Coffee and Tea Authority, told Reuters sales for the first three months of the crop year were 4,000 tonnes more than for the same period the previous year.
He said the 36,907 tonnes was part of the 108,000 tonnes of coffee, a new record for exports, which Ethiopia planned to export in 1996/97 to earn about $236 million from abroad.
Ethiopia's private coffee exporters have pledged to export up to 60,000 of the planned 108,000 tonnes of coffee in 1996/97.

"There is no doubt in my mind private coffee firms will export up to 60,000 tonnes of coffee during the current 1996/97 crop year (October/September)," said Abdul Razak Sherif, chairman of the private Ethiopian Coffee Exporters Association.
Ethiopia exported 102,000 tonnes of coffee in 1995/96 and earned $279.5 million -- lower than the $300.9 million it received for exporting 78,420 tonnes of coffee in 1994/95.
Government coffee officials and private exporters blamed poor global prices for the fall in Ethiopia's export earnings.
Ethiopia is Africa's third largest producer of coffee after Uganda and Ivory Coast. Coffee is Ethiopia's main export commodity and provides about 60 percent of its foreign exchange revenue.
